newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee slightly down vs fwd dlr, spot quiet.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee slightly down vs fwd dlr, spot quiet.

text.p: The Indian rupee was marginally down against the forward dollar in early Thursday trade and dealers said they expected premiums to trade in a narrow range during the day.
They said premiums rose briefly as some banks swapped their sold positions.
"The Reserve Bank of India bought May dollars yesterday," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Premiums are slightly up in anticipation of they (RBI) coming to the market again."
"The bulk of the business is banks' swap operations," he said.
November-delivery dollars were quoted at a premium of 86/89 paise against Wednesday's close of 85/87.
In the spot market, the rupee was stuck in a narrow groove with little dollar demand, dealers said.
"The RBI has not yet come to the market," said a dealer. "We will not see any action until they start buying."
In latest deals, the dollar was quoted 35.817/827 rupees against the previous day's close of 35.820/825.
